name: Question 20
worked_solution:
The integral is defined over the type I region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,2{x}^{2}\le y\le {x}^{2}+1}.$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}x\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2{x}^{2}}^{{x}^{2}+1}x\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2{x}^{2}}^{{x}^{2}+1}x\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[{\int }_{2{x}^{2}}^{{x}^{2}+1}dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[y]_{2{x}^{2}}^{{x}^{2}+1}dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x({x}^{2}+1-2{x}^{2})dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x(1-{x}^{2})dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x-{x}^{3})dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-{x}^{3})dx & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The integral is defined over the type I region D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,2x2≤y≤x2+1}.

So, we can express the integral as follows:

∬DxdA=∫01∫2x2x2+1xdydx

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to y, treating x as a constant:

∫01∫2x2x2+1xdydx=∫01x[∫2x2x2+1dy]dx=∫01x[y]2x2x2+1dx=∫01x(x2+1−2x2)dx=∫01x(1−x2)dx=∫01(x−x3)dx

Then, we integrate with respect to x:

∫01(x−x3)dx=[x22−x44]01=12−14−0=14
